answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake, slashed on proven fraud, held in a shared lagoon of collateral every participant can inspect. Reputation accrues only to identities with a long, costly history, so a fresh fake at the zenith of a hype cycle has no standing and must pay the full stake again for each new face. Ivory-tower defenses fail because they trust paperwork; stake plus verifiable work history makes each extra identity expensive, so an attacker wanting a thousand voices must fund a thousand stakes and wait out a thousand histories.
